summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old female with a history of type 1 diabetes, stage 4 chronic kidney disease, prior pancreas and kidney transplants, and recent mechanical mitral valve replacement was admitted for shortness of breath due to a large left pleural effusion. She had an elevated INR from warfarin, requiring reversal with vitamin K and bridging with heparin before a thoracentesis could be performed. The procedure was successfully completed, removing 1.2 liters of fluid, and her breathing improved. However, imaging showed reaccumulation of the effusion and new left lower lobe consolidation, prompting antibiotic treatment and diuretic adjustment for underlying heart failure. Her INR was stabilized, warfarin was restarted, and she was discharged with follow-up planned for ongoing management of heart failure, anticoagulation, and transplant-related complications.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure
Heart valve replaced by other means
Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type I [juvenile type], not stated as uncontrolled
